wineries.name: Seppeltsfield
wineries.specialty: The 1851 estate where a barrel of Tawny from every year since 1878 still sleeps
wineries.description: The grandest wine estate in Australia: palm-lined avenues, the unbroken Centennial Cellar of Tawnys back to 1878, artisan studios and the Fino restaurant.
wineries.story: Joseph and Johanna Seppelt founded their village-sized estate in 1851, and by 1878 son Benno had begun laying down a barrel of Tawny every single year — a line never broken since, making Seppeltsfield the only winery on Earth that can pour you a wine exactly one century old. The date palms that line the roads were planted by estate workers kept employed through the Great Depression. Today the 1888 gravity-flow winery hums again, the JamFactory studios house glassblowers and knife-makers, and Fino serves one of regional Australia's celebrated lunches.

briefing.icebreaker: There is a barrel of Tawny in the Centennial Cellar for every year since 1878 — no other winery on the planet can say that.
briefing.proMove: Book the Centenary Tour and taste the wine from your birth year straight from the barrel. Bookings are essential for everything here.
briefing.hiddenGem: The palm avenue was a Depression-era job-keeping project — the Seppelts paid workers in food and wages to plant palms rather than lay them off.

wineries.sommNote: Do one fortified tasting even if you think you don't like Tawny. A hundred years in oak makes an argument no one wins against.

wineries.name: Two Hands Wines
wineries.specialty: For the love of Shiraz — garden-series icons poured in a stone cellar door with Highland cattle outside
wineries.description: Founded in 1999 with the mission of making the best possible Shiraz, Two Hands built a global cult following — and keeps Highland cattle in the home paddock.
wineries.story: Michael Twelftree and Richard Mintz started Two Hands in 1999 with a name that described the deal — two mates, hands on everything — and a single-minded devotion to Shiraz. The Garden Series, each wine named for a family member's garden, became one of the most internationally awarded Australian ranges of its era. The stone cellar door at Marananga looks over the home vineyard, and the resident fold of Highland cattle has become nearly as photographed as the wines.

image.alt: The stone cellar door at Two Hands Wines, Marananga
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-13, viewed: stone cottage cellar door with flag and gardens

briefing.icebreaker: Every Garden Series wine is named for a real garden — Bella's belongs to Michael Twelftree's daughter.
briefing.proMove: Walk-ins work on weekdays, but the flagship flights reward a booking; ask for the Garden Series comparison.
briefing.hiddenGem: Say hello to the Highland cattle in the home paddock — the shaggy Scots are the unofficial mascots and they know it.

wineries.sommNote: Tasting Bella's Garden against Angels' Share is a masterclass in how price and polish differ within one grape, one valley, one house.

wineries.name: Torbreck Vintners
wineries.specialty: RunRig and the great dry-grown old-vine Rhône tradition, in a hillside stone cellar
wineries.description: Built on ancient dry-grown vineyards and Rhône conviction, Torbreck's RunRig stands among Australia's most celebrated Shirazes; the stone hillside cellar overlooks Marananga.
wineries.story: David Powell founded Torbreck in 1994, naming it for the Scottish forest where he'd worked as a lumberjack, and set about coaxing greatness from the Barossa's neglected, dry-grown old vines. RunRig — Shiraz with a whisper of Viognier — became a global icon almost immediately, and the whole range still reads like a love letter to the northern Rhône written in Barossa dirt. The cellar door, a beautiful stone barn on the Marananga hillside, keeps the wood-and-iron honesty of the farm buildings it grew from.

image.alt: Torbreck's stone hillside cellar at Marananga
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-13, viewed: stone barn cellar door with open door and vineyard outlook

briefing.icebreaker: Torbreck is a lumberjack's word — David Powell named the winery for the Scottish forest he once felled trees in.
briefing.proMove: Book the Collector's tasting if RunRig is on your list; the standard flight is generous but the icons live upstairs.
briefing.hiddenGem: Almost everything here is dry-grown — no irrigation — from vineyards up to 160 years old. Ask which block is oldest; the answer keeps changing as they find more.

wineries.sommNote: Woodcutter's is the people's Torbreck and brilliant for it, but RunRig with a decade of age belongs on any serious drinker's list.

wineries.name: Hentley Farm
wineries.specialty: The Beauty, The Beast and a degustation restaurant in the 1880s stables
wineries.description: A single-estate farm on Greenock Creek making some of the valley's most awarded Shiraz, with a celebrated destination restaurant in the old stables.
wineries.story: Keith and Alison Hentschke bought a rundown farm on the banks of Greenock Creek in 1997, guided by an 1841 soil map of the colony that marked this bend of red clay over limestone as special. The vineyards they planted produced The Beauty and The Beast — two faces of one hillside — and Clos Otto, the tiny block that became one of the Barossa's most decorated Shirazes. The restaurant in the 1880s stables serves a surprise degustation that made Hentley Farm a dining destination in its own right; reservations are essential for everything.

image.alt: The Hentley Farm restaurant and cellar door among the gums, seen through the vines
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-13, viewed: farm buildings through vine rows, venue-scale

briefing.icebreaker: The Hentschkes chose this land off an 1841 colonial soil map — the surveyors marked this creek bend as prime before a single vine existed.
briefing.proMove: Reservations are essential, cellar door included. If you book one degustation in the Barossa, the stables restaurant is the one.
briefing.hiddenGem: The Beauty and The Beast grow on the same hill — the names describe the plusher and wilder side of one slope, and tasting them together proves it.

wineries.sommNote: Clos Otto is the trophy, but The Beast at half the price loses very little in the translation.

wineries.name: Elderton Wines
wineries.specialty: Command Shiraz from 1894 vines, tasted on the verandah of a heritage homestead
wineries.description: The Ashmead family's heritage homestead at Nuriootpa pours Command Shiraz from vines planted in 1894 — and keeps a grass tennis court for visitors in summer.
wineries.story: When Neil and Lorraine Ashmead took on a neglected Nuriootpa property in 1982, the estate's 1894 Shiraz block came with it. They named its wine Command, and it became one of the Barossa's blue-chip bottles; today brothers Cameron and Allister run the show with the same block at its heart. The cellar door fills a gracious old homestead wrapped in verandahs and gardens, complete with a grass tennis court you can actually book in summer — whites optional, wine compulsory.

image.alt: The homestead cellar door at Elderton Wines, Nuriootpa
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-12, viewed: heritage homestead and gardens, venue-scale

briefing.icebreaker: The Command vineyard went in the ground in 1894 — the Ashmeads inherited it with the farm and built the whole house style around it.
briefing.proMove: Weekends open at 11am, weekdays at 10am. In summer, book the grass tennis court slot at 11am or 1pm and make an afternoon of it.
briefing.hiddenGem: Kangaroos graze between the vines at dusk along Tanunda Road — the verandah is the viewing platform.

wineries.sommNote: Command against Ashmead is the estate in two bottles: 1894 Shiraz power beside polished single-vineyard Cabernet restraint.

wineries.name: Kalleske Wines
wineries.specialty: Certified organic and biodynamic old-vine wines from a family farming Greenock since 1853
wineries.description: Seven generations of Kalleskes have farmed at Greenock since 1853; the winery is fully certified organic and biodynamic, with Grenache vines dating to 1935.
wineries.story: The Kalleske family have worked the same Greenock farm since 1853, and the vineyard has been farmed organically for decades — certification just caught up with habit. Brothers Troy and Tony opened the winery in 2004, turning fruit their family had sold to the region's great houses for 150 years into wines under their own name. The Old Vine Grenache comes off 1935 plantings, Clarry's GSM honours their grandfather, and the cellar door in Greenock's main street pours it all with farm-kitchen warmth. It carries the highest Google rating of any major Barossa cellar door.

image.alt: Shiraz vines on the Kalleske farm at Greenock

briefing.icebreaker: Seven generations on one farm since 1853 — and every vine is certified organic and biodynamic, cow horns and all.
briefing.proMove: Ask what's open from the small-batch range; the cellar door often pours single-block wines that never leave Greenock.
briefing.hiddenGem: Clarry's GSM is named for grandfather Clarence, who ran the farm through the years when Grenache was nearly worthless — the blend is his vindication.

wineries.sommNote: The 1935 Old Vine Grenache is the sleeper buy of the northern valley: ninety-year-old vines, biodynamic farming, and change from a hundred dollars.

wineries.name: Yalumba
wineries.specialty: Australia's oldest family-owned winery, with its own cooperage and the clock tower to prove it
wineries.description: Founded in 1849 and still owned by the same family, Yalumba remains the grand old house of Angaston — the only southern-hemisphere winery with its own working cooperage.
wineries.story: English brewer Samuel Smith planted his first vines by moonlight in 1849 after his day's work, naming the place Yalumba — 'all the land around' in the local language. Five generations of Hill-Smiths later, it is Australia's oldest family-owned winery, with its own nursery, its own cooperage — the only one at a southern-hemisphere winery — and a clock-tower courtyard that has watched 175 vintages arrive. The Signature, a Cabernet-Shiraz blend honouring a chosen Yalumba personality each vintage, is one of the country's most storied wines.

image.alt: The vine-covered pergola and clock tower at Yalumba's Wine Room, Angaston
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-13, viewed: pergola terrace with clock tower, venue-scale

briefing.icebreaker: Samuel Smith planted his first vines by moonlight in 1849, working his brewery job by day — the family still owns every share.
briefing.proMove: Book the Cooperage Tour: watching barrels being toasted over open flame before you taste what they do to Octavius is worth the morning. Mondays open at 11am.
briefing.hiddenGem: Every vintage of The Signature is dedicated to a person who shaped Yalumba — ask whose signature is on the current release and you'll get a life story with your pour.

wineries.sommNote: The Octavius ages in unique octave barrels from their own cooperage — no other Shiraz in Australia can copy the recipe, because no one else owns the tools.

wineries.name: Henschke
wineries.specialty: Hill of Grace — six generations of family winemaking in the Eden Valley high country
wineries.description: The Henschke family's Keyneton cellars pour Australia's most revered single-vineyard Shiraz, from vines planted in the 1860s beside a stone Lutheran church.
wineries.story: Johann Christian Henschke, a Silesian stonemason, made his first wine at Keyneton in 1868; six generations later Stephen and Prue Henschke steward the estate, and their Hill of Grace — from the Grandfathers block planted in the 1860s opposite the Gnadenberg church — trades places with Grange in arguments about Australia's greatest wine. The cellar door occupies the property's 1950s woolstore, and the high, cool Eden Valley hills around it grow Rieslings as crystalline as the Shiraz is profound. Closed Sundays; the drive out through Keyneton is part of the pilgrimage.

image.alt: The Henschke cellar door at Keyneton, Eden Valley
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-12, viewed: cellar door exterior, venue-scale

briefing.icebreaker: Hill of Grace is a translation of Gnadenberg, the Lutheran church across the road from the vines — the Grandfathers block dates to the 1860s.
briefing.proMove: Closed Sundays, and the Hill of Grace Experience books out well ahead — reserve before you plan the rest of your Eden Valley day.
briefing.hiddenGem: The tasting room is the farm's original 1950s woolstore, and the drive from Angaston over the ranges is the prettiest twenty minutes in the region.

wineries.sommNote: If Hill of Grace is beyond the day's budget, Mount Edelstone from 1912 vines is a legitimate icon in its own right — and the Julius Riesling shows why Eden Valley whites belong in the same sentence.

wines.name: Para 21 Year Old Vintage Tawny
wines.description: Two decades in the Seppeltsfield cellars — rancio, roasted walnut, burnt toffee and a finish that simply declines to stop.
wines.sommNote: The gateway drug to the Centennial Cellar. Taste this, then ask what a century does.

wines.name: Seppeltsfield Shiraz
wines.description: Estate Shiraz from the western ridge — dark, generous Marananga fruit raised in the resurrected 1888 gravity winery.
wines.sommNote: Made in a winery where the grapes still move by gravity, exactly as Benno Seppelt designed it.

wines.name: Bella's Garden Shiraz
wines.description: The flagship of the Garden Series — opulent Barossa Shiraz with polish, perfume and the swagger that made Two Hands famous worldwide.
wines.sommNote: The wine that put Two Hands on every international list; drinks like a velvet argument.

wines.name: Gnarly Dudes Shiraz
wines.description: Named for the gnarled old vines it comes from — juicy, spicy, unapologetically generous everyday Barossa Shiraz.
wines.sommNote: The entry point with the best name in the valley. Chill it faintly in summer.

wines.name: Angels' Share Shiraz
wines.description: Named for the wine the barrels lose to evaporation — plush McLaren-meets-Barossa styling with dark chocolate and sweet spice.
wines.sommNote: The crowd-pleaser of the range; the angels have good taste.

wines.name: RunRig
wines.description: Torbreck's monument — old dry-grown Shiraz co-fermented with a whisper of Viognier, vast yet weightless, one of Australia's defining wines.
wines.sommNote: A once-a-decade bottle for most of us. If the Collector's tasting has it open, do not hesitate.

wines.name: Woodcutter's Shiraz
wines.description: The lumberjack's homage — pure, unoaked-feeling old-vine Shiraz drinking far above its station.
wines.sommNote: The best-value serious Shiraz in the valley, and the winemakers know it.

wines.name: The Steading
wines.description: Torbreck's southern-Rhône soul — old bush-vine Grenache, Mataro and Shiraz in savoury, earthy harmony.
wines.sommNote: The wine to convince a Châteauneuf devotee the Barossa speaks fluent Rhône.

wines.name: The Beauty Shiraz
wines.description: The plusher face of the Hentley Farm hill — silky Shiraz with a lick of Viognier, all perfume and polish.
wines.sommNote: Taste it immediately before The Beast; the hill explains itself.

wines.name: The Beast Shiraz
wines.description: The wilder side of the same slope — deeper, darker, more brooding Shiraz with real muscle beneath the fruit.
wines.sommNote: Loses very little to Clos Otto at a fraction of the price. The clever buy.

wines.name: Clos Otto
wines.description: The tiny creek-flat block that made Hentley Farm's name — dense, seamless, decorated Shiraz of remarkable purity.
wines.sommNote: Named for Otto, the farm dog buried in the vineyard. The wine is a worthy memorial.

wines.name: Command Single Vineyard Shiraz
wines.description: From the estate's 1894 block — commanding indeed, with black fruit, dark chocolate and three decades of blue-chip pedigree.
wines.sommNote: One of the Barossa's true single-vineyard aristocrats; the 1894 vines do the talking.

wines.name: Ashmead Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.description: The family-name Cabernet — blackcurrant, cedar and fine-grained tannin, proof of Nuriootpa's quiet Cabernet excellence.
wines.sommNote: Regularly outscores far pricier Coonawarras in blind lineups. The family put their name on the right wine.

wines.name: Greenock Shiraz
wines.description: Organic, biodynamic single-district Shiraz from the family farm — dark plum, earth and unforced generosity.
wines.sommNote: Seven generations of soil knowledge in a bottle that costs less than dinner.

wines.name: Old Vine Grenache
wines.description: From 1935 plantings farmed biodynamically — raspberry, dried herbs and silky, weightless length.
wines.sommNote: Ninety-year-old vines, organic farming, honest price. The northern valley's quiet triumph.

wines.name: Clarry's GSM
wines.description: Named for grandfather Clarence — bright, juicy, organic GSM made for the table rather than the trophy shelf.
wines.sommNote: The picnic red of the Barossa. Clarence would approve of both the wine and the price.

wines.name: The Signature Cabernet & Shiraz
wines.description: The great Australian blend at its most storied — each vintage dedicated to a person who shaped Yalumba, structured to outlive us all.
wines.sommNote: Cabernet's frame, Shiraz's heart — the blend Australia gave the world, from the house that never sold out.

wines.name: The Octavius Old Vine Shiraz
wines.description: Old-vine Barossa Shiraz aged in unique 'octave' barrels from Yalumba's own cooperage — inky, spiced and inimitable.
wines.sommNote: No one else can make this wine: the barrels are built, toasted and coopered on site.

wines.name: Samuel's Collection Bush Vine Grenache
wines.description: Old bush-vine Grenache in the bright, modern register — cherry, spice and gentle grip, named for the founder.
wines.sommNote: The bottle to serve people who claim they don't like Grenache. Watch them recant.

wines.name: Hill of Grace
wines.description: Australia's most revered single vineyard — 1860s vines opposite the Gnadenberg church, in a wine of impossible perfume and calm.
wines.sommNote: Grange's only true rival, and the argument is settled vineyard versus blend. This is the vineyard's case.

wines.name: Mount Edelstone
wines.description: Single-vineyard Eden Valley Shiraz from 1912 plantings — sage, blackberry and granite-edged elegance.
wines.sommNote: In most families this would be the icon. Here it's merely magnificent.

wines.name: Julius Riesling
wines.description: Eden Valley Riesling at altitude — lime blossom, crushed slate and a crystalline line that keeps for decades.
wines.sommNote: The proof that Eden Valley means Riesling as surely as it means Shiraz.
